title: Microsoft Purview DLP: SLA-based alert reporting dashboard
summary: The briefing accurately separates the planned SLA dashboard from existing DLP alert management, and its dates match the roadmap. Two existing-control paths stop at the correct section or list rather than the final setting; these are minor corrections, not publication blockers.

claims.quote: Microsoft Purview: Data Loss Prevention - SLA Based Alert Reporting Dashboard

claims.claim: Microsoft Learn does not yet describe this specific SLA dashboard, so its described behaviour rests on the roadmap.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview SLA dashboard MTTA MTTR licensing default; Purview MTTA MTTD MTTR. Opened dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started, dlp-alerts-get-started, dlp-learn-about-dlp and purview-reports; none describes this dashboard.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview SLA alert dashboard enable default. Read the roadmap and opened dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started, dlp-alerts-get-started and purview-reports; no SLA-dashboard default or enablement requirement was stated.

claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP SLA reporting dashboard tenant policy; Purview SLA SLAs dashboard PowerShell. Opened the DLP alerts and dashboard getting-started pages and Set-DlpComplianceRule; no custom-SLA configuration scope was stated.

claims.claim: The existing DLP Alerts dashboard is at Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Alerts.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention. 2. Select Alerts to view the DLP Alerts dashboard.

claims.claim: Analysts can view DLP alerts in the existing DLP Alerts dashboard.
claims.quote: You use the DLP alert management dashboard in the Microsoft Purview portal to view alerts, events, and associated metadata for DLP policy violations.

claims.claim: Analysts can filter the existing dashboard's alert list.
claims.quote: Use the Filter fields to refine the list of alerts.

claims.claim: The existing dashboard supports assigning ownership of an alert.
claims.quote: After you investigate the alert, return to the Overview tab where you can View details to triage and manage the disposition of the alert, add comments and assign ownership of the alert.

claims.claim: An analyst can set an existing alert's Status to Resolved.
claims.quote: After you take the required action for the alert, set the Status of the alert to Resolved.

claims.claim: Existing alert event details include the sensitive information types detected in the policy match.
claims.quote: sensitive information types (SIT) detected | SITs that were detected as part of the DLP policy match | all events

claims.claim: Existing DLP posture reports are in preview.
claims.quote: Information Protection posture reports, Data Loss Prevention posture reports, and Custom posture reports are in preview.

claims.claim: DLP posture reports in the Microsoft Purview portal include most triggered DLP rules and activities.
claims.quote: You find Posture Reports in the Microsoft Purview portal: ... Data Loss Prevention > Reports ... Data Loss Prevention posture reports ... Most triggered DLP rules and activities

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Posture report data uses a 30-day rolling window.
claims.quote: The data shown in posture reports is gathered on a 30-day rolling-window basis. Save any reports (as .PDF) that you want to keep for future reference.

claims.claim: The cited existing alert and posture-report pages do not describe SLA targets or time-to-respond metrics.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview SLA dashboard MTTA MTTR; Purview MTTA MTTD MTTR. Read dlp-alerts-dashboard-get-started, dlp-alerts-get-started, dlp-learn-about-dlp and purview-reports; no SLA targets or response-time metrics were stated on these pages.

claims.claim: The rule-severity path is Microsoft Purview portal > Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule > Incident reports.
claims.quote: Choose Edit policy. ... Go to the Customize advanced DLP rules page and edit the Low volume of content detected scenarios U.S. PII Data Enhanced. ... Scroll down to the Incident reports section
claims.fix: Extend the front-matter and rendered path to 'Data loss prevention > Policies > policy > Edit policy > Customize advanced DLP rules > rule > Incident reports > Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports'. Set ui.docs to https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/dlp-create-policy-spo-odb-external, which documents the final setting. Keep the existing endpoint procedure as the source for reaching and editing the rule.

claims.claim: Set-DlpComplianceRule -Identity <rule> -ReportSeverityLevel High changes the rule's reporting severity to High.
claims.quote: The Identity parameter specifies the DLP rule that you want to modify. ... The ReportSeverityLevel parameter specifies the severity level of the incident report for content detections based on the rule. Valid values are: ... High

claims.claim: The severity setting under Incident reports is labelled 'Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports'.
claims.quote: Under Incident reports: 1. Set Use this severity level in admin alerts and reports to Low.

claims.claim: Rule reporting severity accepts None, Low, Medium and High.
claims.quote: Valid values are: - None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured. - Low: This value is the default. - Medium - High

claims.claim: None cannot be selected when a DLP rule has no configured actions.
claims.quote: None: You can't select this value if the rule has no actions configured.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Governance controls; Risk assessment: Change & support
claims.claim: Microsoft has not described how SLA targets map to a DLP rule's severity setting.
claims.quote: Searched: Purview DLP SLA reporting dashboard metrics calculation; Purview SLA alert dashboard API Graph PowerShell configuration. Read roadmap, Set-DlpComplianceRule and DLP alert pages; none specifies a mapping from ReportSeverityLevel to SLA calculations.

claims.claim: Microsoft Purview role-group membership management is reached through Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups.
claims.quote: Go to Settings > Roles and scopes to view and manage compliance and governance roles in your organization. 2. Select Role groups.
claims.fix: Extend the front-matter and rendered path to 'Settings > Roles and scopes > Role groups > Role groups for Microsoft Purview solutions > role group > Edit > Edit members of the role group > Choose users', as documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/purview/purview-permissions. The current path reaches the correct role-group list but stops before membership editing.

claims.claim: Add-RoleGroupMember -Identity "<role-group>" -Member "<user-UPN>" adds a user to a role group.
claims.quote: Use the Add-RoleGroupMember cmdlet to add members to a management role group. ... The Identity parameter specifies the role group to add a member to. ... User ID or user principal name (UPN)

claims.claim: The documented procedure for changing role-group membership in the Microsoft Purview portal requires an account assigned Role management.
claims.quote: Sign in to the Microsoft Purview portal by using credentials for an admin account assigned the Role management role.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: Organisations with a DLP subscription listed as E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, G3 or G5 can configure single-event alerts.
claims.quote: Single-event alert configuration: All organizations with a DLP subscription (E1, E3, E5, F1, G1, E3, G3, E5, G5) can configure policies to generate an alert for every time a triggering activity occurs.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: A5, E5 or G5 is one documented route to aggregated alert configuration.
claims.quote: Aggregated alert configuration: To configure aggregate alert policies based on a threshold, you must have either of the following configurations: - An A5 subscription - An E5 or G5 subscription

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The alternative aggregated-alert route is E1, F1, G1, E3 or G3 with Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection Plan 2, Microsoft Purview Suite, or the Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license.
claims.quote: An E1, F1, or G1 subscription or an E3 or G3 subscription that includes one of the following features: - Office 365 Advanced Threat Protection Plan 2 - Microsoft Purview Suite (formerly known as Microsoft 365 E5 Compliance) - Microsoft 365 eDiscovery and Audit add-on license
